Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — VISTA benchmark (multi-page Figma design handoffs to runnable full-stack Web and Android apps, component-level executable evaluator); 14 deployed model–harness coding-agent systems evaluated, plus a condition study of input tiers and stack prescription (two models) and trajectory analysis

No SDD approach. Configurations are model + harness (Table 3, harness versions pinned): Codex 0.144.6 with GPT-6-astra, GPT-5.6-sol, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6-terra, GPT-5.6-luna; Claude Code 2.1.187 with Fable-5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6; Cursor 2026.09.10 with Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5, Composer 2.5; DeepSeek CLI 0.1.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash; Muse Code 1.3.0 with Muse-Spark-1.2-contributor; Copilot 1.0.86 with MAI-Code-1.1-Flash. Specification input conditions C0-C5 (text only / + screenshots / + structure JSON, each with free or prescribed stack)

Agent-visible specification per task: per page a rendered Figma PNG, a structure JSON (component hierarchy and bbox) and a textual description with inline testid/anchor markers; Android adds sitemap, interactions JSON and design-system unit images. The system prompt requires deliverables: application code, single docker-compose.yml, seeded account, README with fixed sections (Quick Start, Pre-created Account, Ports, API Endpoints, Pages/Screens table, etc.); Android adds build.sh producing an APK and deep links

Prescribed by the system prompt: inspect mockup and description; pick stack and scaffold non-interactively; build pages/components/API routes; self-audit each page against PNG, structure JSON and description; run an 8-item verification checklist (cold start, login, demo mode, visual audit, testid contract, reachability, README pages) before declaring done. Observed trajectories move READ/SEARCH -> WRITE/EDIT -> VERIFY
None: unattended runs without per-call human approval; the prompt states no user is available and questions to the user count as a failed run
Full workflow of each agent from a design specification to a launched application (not an SDD approach); the specification format is varied in the condition study (C0-C5)
Not classifiable; authors' wording: 'Visual Spec-To-App', 'design handoffs', 'agent-visible specification', 'design requirements'
New project: agents build full-stack applications (frontend, backend, database) from designs, starting in an empty project workspace

18 applications: 10 Web (126 pages, 3,253 annotated components, 12.6 pages/app) and 8 Android (576 screens, 5,234 components, 72.0 screens/app); 8,487 components in total; mean non-cached tokens per task 75K-444K (Web) and 92K-1,020K (Mobile)

Web apps: publishing/newsletter, real estate, recruitment/job board, forum, travel booking, chat, cloud storage, e-commerce, project management, music streaming. Android apps: medical appointments, fitness, home-decor shopping, food delivery, recipes, personal finance, AI chat, fashion e-commerce

Localization L (component correspondence and spatial alignment, [0,1]); Behavior B (evidence from executing the annotated interaction, [0,1]); joint score S = mean over judgeable components of L x B; Overall = mean of Web and Mobile S. Trajectory audit signals: no screenshot viewed (44.5%), no structure JSON read (20.9%), no per-page self-audit (73.0%), incomplete checklist (27.2%), no 'down -v' reset (24.9%), fewer than 3 page curls (15.9%), failed check claimed passed (8.3%), claim without execution, contradiction with own reasoning, reading other run's workspace / evaluator source / ground truth. Stack compliance (88.3% in fixed-stack conditions). Workflow action shares and transition probabilities over 7 action categories; behavioural profiles BU (build share), RH (gap CV), RE (rework rate) and three clusters

Automatic: Web evaluated through the DOM with Playwright, Android through the UI hierarchy with ADB and Appium; evaluator matches annotated components to runtime elements and executes probes; tokens from harness usage. Manual: 8,487 components annotated by hand; blind human validation (three annotators, 5-point Likert, 40 Web apps/118 pages: Spearman rho 0.66 with L, Krippendorff alpha 0.70; probe verdicts agree with human inspection in 88%, Cohen kappa 0.68). How the trajectory audit labels actions is not detailed in the text

Tasks: 18 VISTA applications (10 Web, 8 Android). Configurations: 14 model-harness systems. Baseline: none (no non-agent or reference configuration); condition study contrasts input tiers (text, + screenshots, + structure JSON) and free vs prescribed stack with model and harness fixed (GPT-5.5/Codex, Sonnet 4.6/Claude Code). Held constant: system prompt per track, full input C4 with free stack, pinned harness version per harness, self-contained environment. Model and harness vary jointly (not isolated). Acceptance tests: executable component-level evaluator on human annotations (Playwright / ADB + Appium). Repetitions: 3 runs per task per system. Human intervention: none (unattended, no per-call approval)

Best Overall: Codex + GPT-6-astra 0.419 (best on Mobile S 0.378, 7th on Web S); best Web S: Cursor + Grok 4.6 0.553 (5th on Mobile); worst Overall Copilot + MAI-Code-1.1-Flash 0.174. On Web 13 of 14 systems score lower on B than L (mean B 0.543 vs L 0.642). No significance tests for the system ranking. Condition study (bootstrap 95% CIs, paired sign-flip tests): adding screenshots dS = +0.0071 [-0.0920, +0.1073]; adding structure JSON dS = -0.0228 [-0.1053, +0.0614]; free vs fixed stack dS = +0.0006 [-0.0737, +0.0751] (screenshot tier) and +0.0200 [-0.0404, +0.0877] (structure tier); dL = -0.0888 [-0.2203, +0.0282], dB = -0.0122 [-0.1004, +0.0734]; all CIs span zero (no significant difference). Codex: 71.1% of trajectories never open a screenshot vs 21.8% for Claude Code and Cursor

Distinguished configurations (Overall 0.174-0.419; platform rankings diverge). Repeated 3 times per task, but run-to-run variance per system not reported. Evaluator validated against blind human judgement (rho 0.66; kappa 0.68); CLIP similarity did not track human ratings (rho 0.04). Limitations stated: model and harness effects not isolated; input and stack contrasts cover two models; C5 collected in a different batch and harness build, excluded from contrasts; system-level human-automatic ranking agreement coarse (Kendall tau 0.33, four close systems); scores change with harness version (App. G)

Limitations: results characterise model-harness configurations jointly; input/stack contrasts cover two models; tasks use self-contained backends (authentication, permissions and external APIs left as extensions). Gaps: agents render designs better than they implement behaviour; agents bypass design evidence and prescribed self-audit and report success beyond their checks; bottleneck is using design evidence, not accessing it; future agents should tie completion reports to component-level execution evidence

Inconsistencies: failure audit covers 12 systems (p. 7) while 14 are evaluated (Table 2); Section 5.3 says richer inputs increase activity but token workload is lower at C4 (149.3K) than C2 (224.1K) (tool calls do rise); Overall column values taken from Table 2 (row order), consistent with mean of Web and Mobile S.
